title: V. Recently discovered peoples listed; whether the West Indies were known to the ancients; Fathers denied antipodes
pass_a_gloss: Joseph Acosta, book 1, chapter 1; Jacob Martin, professor belonging toward Wittenberg, Miscellaneous Disputations, folio 599; as Salmuth thought in his notes on Panciroli's New Discoveries, chapter 1 — and that it had still lain hidden in the secret belonging toward the divine mind. Indeed the constant opinion belonging toward those who asserted antipodes was that their region stood as wholly unknown toward us — in Cicero, On the Republic book 6, and Pomponius Mela book 1, chapter 1. The holy Fathers once denied antipodes — Lactantius, Divine Institutes book 3, chapter 24; Augustine, City of God book 16, chapter 9. Yet it stands as not a curious question whether those regions which we now mark with the title belonging toward the West Indies stood as known toward the ancient Greeks, Romans, and other nations. I call these newly discovered. V. The recent and newly discovered, such as the Guineans, Chinese, Peruvians, Mexicans, Guianans, Tupinamba, Brazilians, and Virginians.
pass_b_english: V. The recent and newly discovered, such as the Guineans, Chinese, Peruvians, Mexicans, Guianans, Tupinamba, Brazilians, and Virginians.

I call these newly discovered. Yet it is not a curious question whether those regions which we now mark with the title of the West Indies were known to the ancient Greeks, Romans, and other nations. The holy Fathers once denied antipodes — Lactantius, Divine Institutes book 3, chapter 24; Augustine, City of God book 16, chapter 9. Indeed the constant opinion of those who asserted antipodes was that their region was wholly unknown to us — in Cicero, On the Republic book 6, and Pomponius Mela book 1, chapter 1 — and that it had still lain hidden in the secret of the divine mind, as Salmuth thought in his notes on Panciroli's New Discoveries, chapter 1; Jacob Martin, professor of Wittenberg, Miscellaneous Disputations, folio 599; Joseph Acosta, book 1, chapter 1.
source_text: V. Nuperi noviterque reperti, ut Guinenses, Chinenses, Peruani, Mexicani, Guianenses, Tououpinambaultii, Brasilenses, Virginienses. Noviter hos dico repertos. Nec tamen curiosa quaestio est, An a veteribus Graecis, Romanisque & aliis gentibus notae fuerint illae, quas nunc Indiae Occidentalis titulo insignimus, regiones? Sancti patres antipodas olim negarunt, Lactantius lib. 3. div. inst. cap. 24. Augustinus lib. 16. de C. D. cap. 9. Quin & constans opinio fuit eorum, qui antipodas asseruerunt, plagam eorum penitus nobis incognitam esse, apud Cic. lib. 6. de rep. & Pomponium Melam lib. 1. cap. 1. & in secreto divinae mentis adhuc delituisse, ut putarunt Salmuthus in notis ad nova reperta Panciroll. cap. 1. Jacobus Martin. profess. Witebergensis disp. miscell. fol. 599. Joseph Acosta lib. 1. cap. 1.
